Subject: Post-call recap + initial POC proposal

Hi Emily / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the charting and discharge-summary workflows. As promised, here’s a short recap and a first-pass POC proposal so we can align expectations before we draft a formal charter.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: generate discharge summaries from encounter notes with 95%+ factual accuracy and reduce MD admin time per discharge by ~30%.
- Volume baseline: ~600 discharges / day across 4 hospitals.
- Data constraints: PHI stays in your VPC; we will run Redwood Private for the trial.

Proposed POC outcomes (high level)
1) Success gates: precision-oriented QA where model passes a clinical fact-check (defined below) on >= 92% of sampled notes, and average end-to-end latency < 2.0s per generated summary under 95th percentile load.
2) Eval cadence: two-week shadow run + offline scorecard on 200 sampled notes -> go/no-go at week 4.
3) Ownership: Greenfield to supply de-identified sample set and clinical reviewers. Redwood to provide inference runtime, model variants, and the scoring rubric.

Open items / asks for you
- Confirm you can supply the 200-sample de-identified gold set by Monday (23 Nov).
- Confirm whether we should score on clinical facts only or include style/readability as a secondary metric.

I’ve attached a draft scoring sheet and a short POC charter (stubs) for your review. If that looks ok, I’ll loop in Ben (CS) and Priyom (Solutions) to finalize the evaluation rubric and timeline.

Best,

Laura Bennett

Hi Laura,

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide the 200-sample set, but it will be de-identified, not fully redacted; PHI tokens will be replaced with stable placeholders (e.g., [PATIENT_NAME_1]). Goal is to preserve clinical context for fact checks.
- For success gates, clinical factuality is the priority. Style/readability matters for clinician adoption, but we want the first pass to focus on correctness and omission errors. We’d set a secondary threshold for readability (mean score >= 3.5/5) but it’s not a blocker.
- Shadow vs offline: we are open to starting with a 2-week offline evaluation (batch scoring) and then a 1-week online shadow in production on a 10% split if offline results are promising. That reduces risk to clinicians.

We’ll aim to deliver the sample set and our initial gold annotations by 24 Nov.

Laura / team,

Attached is a one-page rubric and scoring flow. Highlights:
- Primary metric: Clinical Fact Precision (CFP) defined as #correct_facts / #evaluated_facts. Pass threshold: >= 0.92 on the 200-sample set.
- Severity tiers: Critical (incorrect medication/dosage, wrong diagnosis), Major (missing acute findings), Minor (stylistic/templating issues). Critical errors count as automatic fail.
- Secondary metrics: Readability (Likert 1-5), Conciseness (tokens trimmed compared to baseline), Latency (95th pct <2.0s).
- Inter-rater agreement: require Cohen’s kappa >= 0.7 across two clinical reviewers; if <0.7, expand to three reviewers and take majority.

Workflow (short)
1) Redwood runs model variants locally on the 200-sample set -> outputs attached to scoring sheet.
2) Greenfield clinicians grade using the scoring sheet in the shared Drive.
3) Redwood aggregates scores and computes pass/fail.

I also included a quick offline vs shadow decision guide recommending offline-first with a subsequent 1-week shadow at 10% traffic if offline CFP >= 0.92 and readability >= 3.5.
